clue.text: Tom's part, to criticise a joiner's tool?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and one part of a cat is its claw
to hammer someone is to attack them verbally

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an actor's role amounts to rubbishing a carpenter's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like an actor or a name, but it is the tomcat, whose claw is one of its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A claw hammer, with its split back for pulling nails, is a standard woodworking tool for carpenters.

clue.text: Train husband to understand business account?

indicators.note: read as 'to under-stand': husband stands under the other pieces, which in a down clue means after them

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A man is told to coach his husband in the finances of a company account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to understand' looks like comprehension, but splits as under-stand: in a down answer the husband's letter stands under the business account.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to train or tutor them, as a sports coach trains a team.

clue.text: Film held up in an old African province before delivery

parts.note: the indefinite article, written in its short form A

indicators.note: the turned film is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa until 1994

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting a word up turns it to read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a net or film is a thin covering layer

explanation.surface: A movie is delayed in a former colonial province of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' looks like delayed, but in a down clue it lifts the film to read upwards, backwards; that turned word sits inside the province just after the article's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal care happens during pregnancy, the period before the baby is delivered.

clue.text: A leading figure in half a dozen unions?

definitions.text: A leading figure in half a dozen unions?

parts.words: A leading figure in half a dozen unions?
parts.note: suggests a trade-union leader, but means a man who was the main party in six marriages: the Tudor king with six wives

explanation.surface: A prominent official serves across six trade unions.
explanation.walkthrough: Unions are marriages here, not labour organisations; the English Tudor king married six times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor monarch famously had six wives, so he led in six matrimonial unions.

clue.text: The high point of a muezzin's calling?

definitions.text: The high point of a muezzin's calling?

parts.words: The high point of a muezzin's calling?
parts.note: seems to mean the peak of a career, but means the literal high place from which the Muslim call to prayer is made

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the summit of a prayer-caller's career might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' is both a vocation and the act of calling out; the muezzin calls from a mosque's tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosque's slender tower is where the muezzin traditionally stands to call the faithful to prayer.

clue.text: Fugitive runs after son in eastern cloak

indicators.note: runs comes after the rest, at the end
the son's letter goes inside the eastern cloak

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A runaway flees after his son, wrapped in an oriental cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive is someone fleeing, one who has got away from captivity.

clue.text: Stare stupidly, wife having become trapped in hole

indicators.note: the wife's letter is caught inside the hole

parts.note: a gap is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A man gapes foolishly after his wife gets stuck in a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is a British informal verb for gaping vacantly at something.

clue.text: Range with five burners, ultimately

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A cooker range is fitted with five gas rings, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests a kitchen stove, backed up by the burners; it is the South American mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American mountain chain is a range, the longest continental one on Earth.

clue.text: Painting of gold salver surrounded by china

indicators.note: the gold and the tray sit inside the friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
or is the heraldic word for gold
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: A painting shows a golden platter edged with porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like porcelain beside the salver; it is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction, and a painting is one form of depicting a subject.

clue.text: Don't interfere! It's a good thing Tommy Stout didn't!

definitions.meaning: an instruction not to meddle with something that is fine as it is

definitions.text: It's a good thing Tommy Stout didn't!
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Ding Dong Bell, Little Tommy Stout pulled the cat out of the well, so luckily he did not ignore it

explanation.walkthrough: Ding Dong Bell is a British nursery rhyme: 'Pussy's in the well... Who pulled her out? Little Tommy Stout.' He went to the well to rescue her.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means refrain from meddling; literally, Tommy Stout chose not to keep away from the well.

clue.text: Radium product identified by knight in suit

indicators.note: the knight goes inside the suit

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A radium by-product is identified by a knight in armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests a suit of armour for the knight; it is a legal suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinon is an isotope of radon formed by radioactive decay in the radium-actinium series.

clue.text: After church, Mercian king departs for good? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: the king piece comes after church
departs takes the place of good, one letter swapping for the other

parts.note: Edgar was king of Mercia before ruling all England
D is the abbreviation for departs, as in timetables

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king leaves church for good, which is tough luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' reads as the British phrase for 'tough luck'; here it is literal, a hard cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar, from Somerset, is a firm English cheese, classed among the hard cheeses.

clue.text: Polish group rejected sexual enticement

parts.note: to hone is to refine or polish

indicators.note: rejected sends the group back, reading it backwards

parts.note: a party is a group of people

explanation.surface: A Polish political faction is said to have turned down sexual lures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeytrap is a scheme that uses sexual attraction to lure a target, as in espionage.

clue.text: Guest abandons appeal for sun screen

indicators.note: the appeal letters are dropped from the guest

parts.note: a guest is a visitor
it means sex appeal

explanation.surface: A guest stops asking to apply suncream.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a peak or shade shielding the eyes from sunlight.

clue.text: Surgeon's companion, a natural climber

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A doctor's partner is a born mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a British honour, Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous plant whose tendrils let it climb, so it is a climber by nature.

clue.text: Dither badly during leave

indicators.note: the badly piece occurs in the middle of leave

parts.note: to vacate is to leave a place
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates poorly while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' suggests holiday time but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver indecisively between options.

clue.text: Dump fruit in river, protecting bank

indicators.note: that combination goes inside the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: the fruit wraps round the bank

parts.note: a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn
a row, as in a bank of seats or keys

explanation.surface: Someone tips fruit into a river, guarding the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverbank in this scene; it is a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to discard it, getting rid of it as unwanted.

clue.text: A new ring? A new description of the old one!

indicators.note: the second new signals the letters are made fresh, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new opera production of The Ring is described in the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: The old ring is the composer's Ring cycle, and the adjective describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the composer of Der Ring des Nibelungen, describing that old cycle.

clue.text: Came together and composed

explanation.definitionFit: Collected means both gathered together and calm, cool and in control of oneself.

clue.text: Work keeping judge in clover, possibly

indicators.note: the work holds the judge inside it

parts.note: toil is hard work
a ref, referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A job keeps a judge living in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in clover' is an idiom for luxury; here 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil, a three-leaved plant, is a name for clover and its relatives.

clue.text: City man turned up and stirred up riot

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reverses the name

parts.note: Ted is a man's name

indicators.note: the riot letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man arrived in the city and incited a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arrival but reverses TED to DET; ROIT is the anagram of RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a large American city in Michigan, the motor city.

clue.text: Like some tender lass following article in French

indicators.note: the lass comes after the article

parts.note: le is the French definite article
gal is an informal word for a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A girl who sounds rather affectionate follows a French grammar point.
explanation.walkthrough: Legal tender is money that must be accepted in payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Some tender is legal: currency that must by law be accepted.

clue.text: Resting in plane after initial take-off

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off

parts.note: travelling in a plane is flying

explanation.surface: Someone is lying back in an aircraft after the first part of take-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means reclining or at rest, as in lying down.

clue.text: Like an order that's mildly sarcastic? Not right

indicators.note: 'Not right' says the abbreviation for right must be absent from the sarcastic word, so it is taken out

parts.note: ironic means wry or mildly sarcastic

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a gently sarcastic command is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Order is a classical order of architecture, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of columns, with scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: Outgoing vicar returning hot, ultimately, after run

indicators.note: the later pieces follow the run

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat

indicators.note: returning sends the word back, reversing it

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar

indicators.note: 'ultimately' means in the end, so only the final letter of the word it governs is kept

explanation.surface: An outgoing vicar comes back from a jog red-hot.
explanation.walkthrough: VER is REV reversed, T the last letter of hot.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert is an outgoing, sociable person; this spelling is a variant.

clue.text: Can a US city appear so badly constructed?

parts.note: a tin is a can
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A question about whether an American city could seem shoddily built.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinny describes something cheap and flimsy, made of thin metal.

clue.text: Woman extravagant over food colouring

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name

indicators.note: over means turned over, reversed

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: A woman goes over the top with food dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is an orange-red dye from achiote seeds used to colour foods like cheese.

clue.text: Neat fellow goes about supported by varsity type

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, an ox
on means about, concerning
Ian is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A tidy man walks around, propped up by a university student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy but is cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxonian is a member of Oxford University, a varsity type.

clue.text: Make an impression in ballet chinois

indicators.note: the letters are found within the two words

explanation.surface: Leave a mark in a Chinese-style ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave, making a lasting mark on a surface.

clue.text: Tall sentry unexpectedly lacking in tidiness

indicators.note: the letters fall into an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: A tall soldier on guard is surprisingly scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatternly means slovenly, untidy and dirty in appearance or habits.
